first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior onboarding/signup simplification evidence directly addresses both signals. Verify memory_86 because it is the closest intervention match, and memory_73 because competitor pricing creates a consequential alternative. I currently favor a guarded onboarding simplification test for sustainable qualified revenue, while preserving uncertainty about whether price pressure requires a pricing response.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding, prioritizing the confirmed result showing +13% completion, 2.1-day faster time-to-value, and +3% 30-day retention. This directly addresses both current completion and activation declines and supports sustainable qualified revenue. Do not pursue targeted promotional pricing this cycle: although it drove +18% qualified revenue initially, 30-day retention fell 12% and the cohort failed to survive renewal. Monitor activation, qualified revenue, and retention by segment; the precise contribution of signup simplification remains less certain because memory_31 was not verified.

final2.rationale: The immediate doubling of churn conversations and deeper competitor cut warrant a narrowly targeted defensive pricing test for demonstrably price-sensitive, at-risk SMB accounts rather than a broad discount. The verified evidence shows that discounting can lift near-term qualified revenue but reduced 30-day retention by 12% and failed at renewal, so apply strict eligibility, duration, margin, renewal, and cohort-retention guardrails. Continue the onboarding improvement as the sustainable baseline, but do not assume it alone will offset acute competitive price pressure.
